title: Web APIs Small Examples
description: Use these small Web APIs examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Read JSON text
examples.description: JSON is a text format for data. JSON.parse turns that text into JavaScript values that code can read.

examples.title: Fetch local data
examples.description: fetch asks for a resource and returns a promise for a response.
examples.output: With a real books.json file at that address, the code prints its parsed data. Missing files produce a handled error.

examples.title: Stop a request
examples.description: AbortController gives a request a stop signal.
examples.output: The request is cancelled if it is still in progress. Its rejection is handled, usually with the name AbortError.

examples.title: Use URL search values
examples.description: URLSearchParams reads and writes query values in an address.
examples.output: The first line is garden club. The query string contains topic=garden+club and level=1.

examples.title: Remember a small browser value
examples.description: localStorage stores small text values for one site in one browser.
examples.output: The console shows 1 where storage is allowed. Otherwise the page gives a handled message.

examples.title: Read a chosen file
examples.description: A file input lets a person choose a file.
examples.output: After a text file is chosen, its words appear in the pre element.

examples.title: Copy text after a click
examples.description: The Clipboard API can write text to the clipboard.
examples.output: On an allowed HTTPS or localhost page, the button copies Garden club. A failure shows a manual-copy message.

examples.title: Ask for a location carefully
examples.description: Geolocation asks the browser for a location.
examples.output: When used after an appropriate user action on a secure page, it reports accuracy or a handled failure.

examples.title: Draw a simple canvas shape
examples.description: Canvas is a drawing area controlled by JavaScript.
examples.code: <canvas id="art" width="240" height="120" aria-label="A blue rectangle">A blue rectangle</canvas><script>const ctx=document.querySelector("#art").getContext("2d");ctx.fillStyle="navy";ctx.fillRect(20,20,100,60);</script>
examples.output: A navy rectangle is drawn 20 units from the left and top, with a width of 100 and height of 60.

examples.title: Watch when a part comes into view
examples.description: IntersectionObserver tells your code when an element crosses a visibility boundary.
examples.code:
Scroll down

You found the note.
examples.output: When the note enters the viewport, the message is logged once and the observer stops watching it.

examples.title: Watch a box size
examples.description: ResizeObserver reports changes to an element's size.
examples.code: A flexible box
examples.output: The console logs the content width when the box is first observed and when that size changes.

examples.title: Move a calculation to a worker
examples.description: A web worker runs JavaScript in another thread.
examples.output: With the two real files served locally, the main page logs 12 and then stops the worker.
